reviews.author: sam
reviews.text: straight up a gorgeous place to stay right off the beach.  Whats frustrating is other campers and poor etiquettes like letting their kids stand in the road as your pulling your trailer by had one reach out and tried to grab the side.  No parents moved from their lounge chair to get there kids. Also if your an out of state veteran don't expect any discount and you have to pay extra for being out of state also it cost 10 bucks to use the dump station lol it all adds up and not cheap.  Dont mind paying a little extra but come on

reviews.author: Bob ROBERTS
reviews.text:
It seems like all Oregon state parks are very well maintained, situated in really nice places, have good facilities, and are reasonably priced.
There is speech access though it is a fairly good hike across the dunes to get there.
There are no sewer hookups at the RV camping area sites. The park has a dump station as you first come in so you can empty as needed.

reviews.author: Kristine Hartman
reviews.text:
Horse camping May 2026 site H10

Nice!

Pipe stalls. Potable water at each site.

Manure pit nearby. Wheelbarrows too.

Clean full flush toilet bathrooms. Showers one camp group over.

Dogs on leash allowed in camp.

Easy access to the beach.

reviews.author: John Mitchell
reviews.text: The campground was very nice overall. Easy to find amenities, access to the beach was convenient, clean, organized campsites. Partially covered picnic table on our deck made making meals better. Our only issue (and the one reason we left a day early) was the mattress pads on the bed and fold down couch. They were too hard, my hips would start to ache (I’m a side sleeper). Not everyone will have the same issue, but when it comes to sleep and camping that’s a deal breaker for us.

reviews.author: Isa Dean
reviews.text: I'm camping with a popup trailer at the comfortable, and beautiful Nahalem State Park Campground. Spacious campsites with loads of green level space for tents or for hanging out. Dogs allowed on leash and off-leash at the beach. Thoughtfully set up with places to deposit dog bags and get additional ones as you're walking through. There's a brand new and especially nice bathroom building near my site (D43). Some sites are shaded (which also protects you from the wind on windy days). Both bathroom and shower buildings were clean and well kept. It feels really nice here, and while you have to climb over what amounts to a large sand dune to get to the beach - what a lovely beach it is. This park is far enough from 101 to be very quiet. Prices are much more reasonable than private RV parks. I enjoyed the new looking water and electric hookups (50A, 20A, 110V). There are warm lights that come on by the hookups at dark and add a bit of charm.

reviews.author: PotatoChipsnDip
reviews.text: Nehalem Bay is a nice, large campground in a convenient location for exploring the northern coast. We spent three nights there, and explored as far north as Ecola State Park and Cannon Beach on one day and the Three Capes route to the south another day. Your campground parking pass is valid at any Oregon state day use areas along the coast, with a few others being national lands that take the America the Beautiful pass. We also walked for miles at Nehalem Bay beach and did the spit trail. It's about 5 miles round trip and is wide with trees on both sides and a few peeks at the water. Once you get to the end of the spit, it is an amazing beach and jetty and we we were the only people there. An extra day to explore the area even more would have been great. This campground has very limited trees or privacy, and we expected that based on what we read about it in advance. The close proximity to the beach made up for that. The bathrooms are brand new with single rooms for toilets and showers. We stayed in D55, which is two sites away from the trash and recycling area. This turned out to be convenient and a positive aspect, and there was a dish water drain right across from the site. The sites are paved and relatively level. The dump station was huge with two dumps and about 15 RV spaces to park afterwards (no one else was there). There was a trash can and restroom at the dump station parking lot too. I would definitely stay here again if in the area.

reviews.author: wish-we-were-here
reviews.text: This is a great park with clean facilities and easy access to the ocean. Sites were well maintained. Nice amenity was the sink water disposal drain through out the park.

reviews.author: Beerboy
reviews.text: Wonderful park, one of the best. About 5 miles from Hwy 101, but road to park is in good shape. Nice trails from the campground to the beach. Sites have average spacing with some trees and hedges in between. 50 amp electric and water were serviceable. Bathrooms were the same as the other Oregon state parks, nothing fancy but usable. Showers had hot water. 3 lanes to park in at the entrance station. You must park and walk to the station. Beach is very walk-able in both directions, we hiked the Nehalem Spit trail and came back on the beach. AT&T cell service was great, 5 bars of 5G, no need for the booster to easily stream. 20+ HDTV channels most of which came in well.

reviews.author: rls1936
reviews.text: This is definitely in our top 10 of our trip. Sites are nicely spaced out. Lots of trees. All sites have electric and water. Paved pad. Almost all sites back up to woods. The dunes and beach are beautiful. Would be great to visit in the summer when it is warm enough to really enjoy. Firewood is available for $5 per bundle. The dump station was adequate although the opening is at a funny angle. A little tough to get the hose elbow seated correctly. Visited the farmers market, the pie shop, the pizza pie shop. Drove north to Cannon Beach to see the haystack rock and ate at Mo's. Wife gave a big thumbs up to the clam chowder. My burger was excellent. Drove south to Tillamook Factory, but so did just about everyone in a 50 mile radius. After seeing the long lines to eat there, we skipped it.

reviews.author: The Willi's
reviews.text: i stayed here over memorial day weekend so everyone and their mom was camping here. the sites are a bit close together which coupled with the fact it was a holiday weekend made it feel a bit crowded. despite that it is an excellent campground! all the sites have full hookups which even as a non rv camper is still nice. the rangers at the check in both were nice and helpful. the bathrooms were clean and the showers were HOT and FREE! there is convenient beach access though it does require walking up a sand dune then down a sand dune which is a bit unpleasant. the walk isn't long but the sand is deep and difficult to walk up hill on. the beach itself is gorgeous and perfect for walking on. i would absolutely stay here again.

reviews.author: Paige16
reviews.text: October – Our 3rd time to Nehalem Bay State Park. The entrance to the park is still very rough and bumpy until you actually reach the park entrance. The roads inside the park are very good, smooth and wide. Our spot B-37 was very nice except the fact of the rain for 2 days that created a pool next to the asphalt our trailer was setting on by the back of the trailer. We used the bathrooms and found the stalls were very tight to close the stall door. You had to stand directly beside the toilet to shut the door. But the bathrooms and showers where very clean and well kept. For that matter the whole park was clean and well kept. We bought take out lunch 2 times at the Riverside Fish & Chips in Nehalem. The fish and fries were cooked to perfection. The outside of the fries were crispy and the inside was very soft, plus the coating on the outside of the fries were excellent. The fish was not greasy, well cooked and juicy on the inside.

reviews.author: Robert Davis
reviews.text: 10 minute walk to miles of fabulous Oregon beach. 15 min drive to great hiking at Oswald West State Park. 25 minute drive to the shops and restaurants in Cannon Beach. Verizon and AT&T cell service excellent! This is great beach camping. The sites are typical size and spacing for an Oregon state park but both inner and outer rings are pretty nice. Not secluded but pretty comfortable. The beach is fabulous for humans and dogs alike. And the view north to Falcon Cape is really nice. We'll be coming back.

reviews.author: Jodie D
reviews.text: Beautiful campground. The walk to the beach is very close and easy. Clean bathrooms. The playground was interesting. It is for older kids or adults not really a playground more like an exercise area.

reviews.author: Jz Smith
reviews.text: Looking at the pictures if would seem that the campsites are really close together. Might as well pitch camp in some city . I gave this campground just one star because of the over crowding.
reviews.title: Title?

reviews.author: Jon
reviews.text: Great campground. It's located right next to the beach. The beach is really long so perfect for walks and/or finding a spot for yourself to enjoy a day at the beach. The campground is well-kept. The restrooms were immaculate and well-stocked. The electrical hook-up to our site worked great. We had no problems charging our Tesla as there is a standard 5-20 outlet(120V/20A) and 14-50(240V/50A) outlet. There's even a 10-30 outlet. You can easily book a reservation online or just show up, find a spot and self-register at the campground. We stayed for 2 nights in our Model Y and the experience was great. The area is really nice.
reviews.title: Great campground

reviews.author: Nancy
reviews.text: Sites are within walking and hearing distance of the ocean waves. Sites are close but there are trees in between for some privacy. Great biking and walking paths. Small airport in the park and we saw a herd of about 20 elk grazing on it during an early October afternoon. Deer in the park that are tame and will eat out of your hand as we saw other campers doing it. Hosts were helpful and the park was very clean. A great place for families. Great beach area.
reviews.title: One Of My Favorites!

reviews.author: Jim Z
reviews.text: To the person who gave this park one star from looking at pictures, you should actually visit before reviewing. The sites aren't bad. Many of the ones on the inner sides are actually quite roomy. There is a lot to explore here.
reviews.title: Great Park.

reviews.author: Leo Ma
reviews.text: We stayed in a yurt at Nehalem Bay State Park in June 2023. It was awesome! They effectively combined the comfort of a cabin and the close to nature that a tent has. The nearby bathhouses were clean and pleasant enough for me. We visited the beach during sunset and it was beautiful. Best part? You can hear the ocean waves in the campground, it was very relaxing and I slept comfortable. Only “thorn” I can name is that the yurts are too close to each other, so I would recommend picking one that is surrounded by trees, or to pick the isolated yurts.
reviews.title: No wonder it’s hard to book a campsite here!

reviews.author: Christina H
reviews.text: Luckily for us, this place is less than an hour drive from our home, but it was an awesome place for just a nice getaway. The facility was great and we even earmarked it for a later visit to bring friends who could stay in the yurts while we were in an RV. There was wildlife viewing and lots of hiking trails along the forest and on the beach.
reviews.title: Great camping spot.

reviews.author: KylieS
reviews.text: This park is very very crowded. Camp sites feel like they are on top of each other. It is a good park for families and large groups. We just didn't like the vibe which had more to do with an obnoxious large group of campers, than the actual campground.
reviews.title: Very crowded camp ground

reviews.author: Fred_Merchant
reviews.text: We stayed in Loop B of the Campground for three nights in a 39 foot motorhome and really enjoyed it. The Campground is adjacent to the beach at the top of the spit that separates Nehalem Bay from the Pacific. It is sheltered by grass covered sand dunes. The Campground has an open feel with large grassy areas populated with shore pines and surrounded by native vegetation. You can enjoy the sun at your site when it’s out. RV sites have 30 Amp power with many of them having 50 Amp power. Potable water spigots are available at all RV sites. Picnic tables and fire pits are provided as well as a source of free firewood. An RV dump station is provided near the registration area. Volunteer Park Hosts can help you with confirming your registration, locating your site, issues, questions, or just to say hello. Beach access is available along prepared paths over the dunes. The sand is loose when dry and clumpy when wet. Do not disturb nest birds, especially Snowy Plovers. The beach is wide open and the sand is firm just above the tide line. It is over 2 miles long so great for a long walk. You can return to the campground along a shared hiking and horse trail closer to Nehalem Bay. The bay is well known for Dungeness Crab and several types of bay clams. Conditions can get muddy though so consider waders for crabbing or clamming. Every loop has bathrooms and showers, so you can conserve water. We really enjoyed our time here. Oregon State Parks are affordable and fill up fast. The only amenity that would make it better would be a sewer connection at the RV sites. But we know the park is protecting the estuary environment.
reviews.title: Well used campground

reviews.author: LostLobstah
reviews.text: Best location, campground, beach. Perfect location off Rte 101. Clean, accommodating, separate camp area for horses. Bike and hiking trails. Great location to day travel and adventure
